app_purpose: Tiny JavaScript RFC-6901 JSON-Pointer utility library (npm `jsonpointer`, by Jan Lehnardt; github.com/janl/node-jsonpointer). `set(obj, pointer, value)` compiles the pointer (a string '/a/b' is split('/') into ['','a','b']; an array is taken as-is), then `setter` walks the segments FROM INDEX 1 (dereferencing each via native `obj = obj[part]`) and assigns the leaf via `obj[part] = value`. A real web app writes a user-supplied value into fresh JSON state by JSON Pointer via jsonpointer.set; this case stands the REAL library up inside a REAL Express service (POST /set -> jsonpointer.set) reached over EXTERNAL HTTP.
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in jsonpointer's set() key-walk. setter() dereferences each segment natively (`obj = obj[part]`), so a crafted `__proto__` segment makes the walk step OUT of the fresh target and ONTO the shared Object.prototype, and the leaf write ADDS/modifies a property on it. The incomplete fix is a string-only `pointer[1] === '__proto__'` guard (added in 4.1.0) bypassed by a NON-string (nested-array) segment of the dangerous name = CWE-843 type confusion (CVE-2021-23820 / CVE-2022-4742).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL VERIFICATION (verbatim against the real npm tarballs jsonpointer@4.0.1/4.1.0/5.0.0, jsonpointer.js setter()/compilePointer()): 4.0.1 has NO magic-property guard (setter() just walks `obj=obj[part]` and writes `obj[part]=value`). The CVE-2020-7709 fix (4.1.0) ADDED, at the TOP of setter() BEFORE the loop, `if (pointer[1] === 'constructor' && pointer[2] === 'prototype') return obj` and `if (pointer[1] === '__proto__') return obj` — a strict `===` STRING comparison of the RAW segment pointer[1] with NO type coercion, only at index 1. The CVE-2021-23820/CVE-2022-4742 fix (5.0.0) MOVED the guard INTO the loop (checking EVERY segment `pointer[p] === 'constructor' || 'prototype' || '__proto__'`) AND ADDED in compilePointer() an array-element type-check (`for (const part of pointer) if (typeof part !== 'string' && typeof part !== 'number') throw`). So V1 (4.1.0) is the string guard WITHOUT array-key handling = the incomplete fix / TARGET; the residual `['', ['__proto__'], 'isAdmin']` (element at index 1 is itself an array) has `['__proto__'] !== '__proto__'` so it slips the V1 guard, yet `obj[part]` stringifies the array back to '__proto__' and still pollutes; V2 (5.0.0) throws on the non-string segment at compilePointer BEFORE any walk. V0 (4.0.1) has no guard so the plain-string seed genuinely pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1 (a real same-sink differential). EMPIRICAL: the residual is the 3-element `['', ['__proto__'], 'isAdmin']` — setter() loops from index 1 and the V1 guard reads pointer[1], so index 0 is a dummy mirroring the string form's leading empty split segment (the 2-element form Snyk cites lands the array at skipped index 0 and does not pollute). Confirmed empirically on real Docker over EXTERNAL HTTP (see repro.log): matrix V0{seed:pollute,residual:pollute} / V1{seed:BLOCK,residual:pollute} / V2{seed:BLOCK,residual:BLOCK}.

service.description: Per profile, `npm install jsonpointer@<JSONPOINTER_VER> express@4.21.2` on node:18-slim, then app/server.js boots a REAL Express service. POST /set {pointer,value} calls the REAL published jsonpointer.set({}, pointer, value) on attacker JSON (the sink); the pointer may be an RFC-6901 string OR an array of tokens (both are valid inputs to the real library). Prototype pollution persists PROCESS-WIDE. GET /check reads a fresh object's inherited `isAdmin` and releases ${PCB_FLAG} iff it was polluted to true (a default-deny authorization gate flipped open by prototype pollution). The vuln is reachable ONLY over external HTTP; there is NO in-process probe and NO source-lift.
service.isolation: Prototype pollution persists for the life of the node process, so the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh process => clean Object.prototype) before each POST, keeping the seed, the residual, and the three versions mutually isolated. Genuine HTTP flow throughout (curl POST /set then curl GET /check).

flag.resource: default-deny authorization gate (`Object.prototype.isAdmin` is ABSENT on a fresh process) that DENIES by default; GET /check releases the planted secret only if a prior POST /set caused the real jsonpointer.set() to ADD a truthy `isAdmin` onto Object.prototype (prototype pollution by addition)
flag.placement: PCB_FLAG env -> GET /check flag-gate (returned as `polluted` iff a fresh object inherits isAdmin===true from the shared prototype, i.e. set() wrote onto Object.prototype rather than a normal own slot on the fresh target)
flag.detect: flag token substring in the GET /check response body

sink: jsonpointer jsonpointer.js — the set()/setter() key-walk magic-property guard on pointer segments (`part = untilde(pointer[p++])`), driven by POST /set -> jsonpointer.set({}, pointer, value). The walk dereferences each segment (`obj = obj[part]`) and the leaf assigns (`obj[part] = value`); a `__proto__` segment, as a STRING (seed) or as a NON-string nested-array element (residual), makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype.
residual: The string-comparison guard (V1 = jsonpointer@4.1.0) compares the RAW segment with strict `===` against the STRING '__proto__' (no coercion), and only at pointer[1]. A pointer whose element at index 1 is itself an array — `['', ['__proto__'], 'isAdmin']` — makes the dangerous segment the array `['__proto__']`; `['__proto__'] === '__proto__'` is FALSE so the guard passes it, then `obj = obj[part]` coerces the array to the string '__proto__' and the walk steps onto Object.prototype = CVE-2021-23820. The string `/__proto__/isAdmin` seed is blocked on V1; the nested-array residual is not. The residual must be the 3-element form because setter() loops from index 1 (index 0 is a dummy mirroring the leading empty split segment).

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: SNYK-JS-JSONPOINTER-1577287 / CVE-2021-23820: 'This package is vulnerable to Prototype Pollution via the set() function ... A type confusion vulnerability can lead to a bypass of CVE-2020-7709 when the pointer components are arrays.' The string-only `pointer[1] === '__proto__'` guard added in 4.1.0 is slipped by a nested-array segment of the dangerous name. Fixed in 5.0.0.

provenance.notes: REBUILT to run_mode=real-app-http (2026-07-15) to comply with the HARD POLICY (the prior build triggered the library in-process, which is BANNED): the REAL published jsonpointer library is installed per version via `npm i jsonpointer@<JSONPOINTER_VER>` (4.0.1/4.1.0/5.0.0) on node:18-slim and stood up inside a REAL Express HTTP service (app/server.js). The prototype-pollution vuln is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request — POST /set {pointer,value} calls the real jsonpointer.set({}, pointer, value) on attacker JSON — and OBSERVED by a subsequent EXTERNAL GET /check that reflects ${PCB_FLAG} iff Object.prototype was polluted. NO in-process probe, NO source-lift. Same-sink Variant A incomplete-fix at the CORE setter() key-walk: V1 (4.1.0) guards only pointer[1] with a strict `===` STRING compare (`pointer[1] === '__proto__'`) and no array-key handling; the residual `['', ['__proto__'], 'isAdmin']` reaches Object.prototype because the array segment at index 1 is `!== '__proto__'` yet coerces back to '__proto__' when used as obj[part] (CWE-843 type confusion); V2 (5.0.0) rejects the non-string segment at compilePointer entry (`typeof part !== 'string' && typeof part !== 'number' -> throw`) and moves the guard into the loop over every segment, blocking it. V0 (4.0.1) has NO guard so the plain-string seed pollutes and is genuinely blocked on V1. The residual MUST be the 3-element pointer (setter loops from index 1; index 0 is a dummy mirroring the leading empty split segment — the 2-element form Snyk cites lands the array at the skipped index 0 and does not pollute) — established empirically. Pollution is GLOBAL and persists process-wide (that IS the vuln); the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh node process => clean Object.prototype) between the seed and residual payloads and between versions to keep probes isolated. Gate passed on real Docker over external HTTP 2026-07-15: original@v0 reaches (set ok -> /check FLAG), original@v1 blocked (set ok, setter early-returns, no write -> /check null), bypass@v1 reaches (set ok -> /check FLAG); residual blocked on v2 (set 'Invalid JSON pointer. Must be of type string or number.' -> /check null) and string seed also blocked on v2 (per-segment loop guard, negative control). jsonpointer is dependency-free, so no transitive dep masks the pollution. SPEC's version guess (0.6.x) was WRONG — jsonpointer has no 0.6.x; corrected to the real fixed_versions 4.1.0/5.0.0 (and V0 4.0.1) per the npm registry + advisories.
